name: Mini Tournament
description: Fill a real four- or eight-player elimination bracket. Only organizer-confirmed winners advance to the next match.
businessHypothesis: Small groups may return for another event after an organizer invites them. Repeated tournament completion is a better demand signal than the number of empty brackets created.

name: Book Companion
description: Create a reading club around four original fictional stories, with chapter discussions and reader-reported progress.
businessHypothesis: A short shared text may lower the barrier to joining a discussion. Return reading and chapter participation must be observed before assuming community or revenue growth.

name: Micro Academy
description: Author mini lessons and quizzes, keep answer keys on the server and unlock learner progress through correct answers and prerequisites.
businessHypothesis: Authors may invite learners to a focused skill lesson. Actual completion and repeat learning can indicate demand; accreditation and revenue are not claimed.

name: Knowledge Relay
description: Solve three generated questions asynchronously as a team, passing the flag to another member after each completed stage.
businessHypothesis: A completed stage invites another participant to return later. Handoff-to-return rate and team completion time can test whether the asynchronous loop works.

name: Creative Partnership
description: Run a time-bounded creative jam through volunteer task claims, deliveries and owner approval or requests for revision.
businessHypothesis: Small projects may bring creative groups back for another jam. Actual deliveries and approvals are necessary evidence before building broader organizational or advertising assumptions.
